en: Distillation is yet another core term
related to large language models and
post-training.
You may have heard about complaints by top,
typically US AI companies,
that other competitors,
especially Chinese competitors, as they put
it, are using a concept or an approach
called distillation to train their models.
And the idea is simple.
You can use an AI model, you can use ChatGPT
to ask it an endless amount of questions and
throw a broad variety of problems at it
and use its output to train your own model
or to improve your own model. So you're
using another model as a teacher model to
train and improve your student model.
Now, that can be much easier and cheaper
than manually collecting all that data from
from the public internet and all that
synthetic data that the top labs used to
improve their models. It can be much cheaper
and easier if you're just using an existing
top model and you are deriving your model
from it. Now,
this process, distillation, is not
necessarily problematic or illegal. The top
AI companies are doing it themselves on
their own models.
You can, for example, produce a cheaper
version of a model by using the more
expensive
complex model as a teacher and deriving a
simpler model from it, a smaller model from
it, for example. So distillation is an
important technique,
but it can also be abused to cut corners or
save some money on training.
